churches.assessment: Chancellor Baptist's doctrinal statement is genuinely solid — they affirm Scripture as God's Word, salvation through Christ alone, eternal security, baptism by immersion, Great Commission evangelism. The church's mission statement (pointing people to Christ and into His church) is clear and healthy. The honest concern is BGAV affiliation: unlike SBC, BGAV is the moderate Virginia Baptist stream that parted ways over inerrancy and women's ordination. That doesn't automatically mean Chancellor is progressive — many BGAV churches are theologically conservative at the local level — but the accountability structure is to a moderate denomination. Before joining, Moop should ask: Does Chancellor have an elder board? What is the stance on women in pastoral roles? Pastor Cameron West's background and convictions are unknown — worth a direct conversation.

churches.assessment: Trinity Episcopal has the same fundamental problem as St. George's Episcopal: it belongs to The Episcopal Church (TEC), which has made formal, binding institutional commitments to LGBTQ+ affirmation that place it outside biblical alignment. The rector lists she/her pronouns on the church website, men serve with he/him pronouns listed — pronoun-aware staff culture is a visible marker of TEC's progressive institutional identity. Founded in 1877, Trinity has a rich liturgical history and likely has sincere Christians in the congregation, but the denominational framework and leadership culture are incompatible with Moop's convictions. The 'inclusive community of seekers' branding further flags a therapeutic/inclusive ecclesiology rather than a word-and-sacrament Great Commission model. Not recommended.
churches.gender_detail: Female rector (she/her pronouns listed); TEC ordains women at all levels and affirms LGBTQ+ clergy and marriage
